I only have 3.5 mu, so I will not do anything fancy. I will plant spring maize on all of it, same as usual, and I will adjust a little from last year. On small land, every bag of fertilizer costs money, but if maize lacks fertilizer, the ears come out small and that loss hurts more. In our place, people around me mostly use hybrid seed now, and if the field has water from a well, the yield can stand up, so I will also use hybrid seed. I will first rotary till the land because it is quicker and cheaper than deep ploughing for my small area, and it is enough for maize. For fertilizer, I will not go too light. I will count about 20 kg nitrogen per mu, 8 kg phosphorus per mu, and 6 kg potassium per mu. Part I will put in as base fertilizer, and the nitrogen I will leave some for topdressing when the maize gets tall, because that is when it really pulls fertilizer. Since I have well irrigation, I will water about 3 times if the season is normal: once after sowing if the soil is dry, once around jointing, and once around tasseling. For pesticides, I will spray about 2 times in a normal year, mainly depending on weeds and insects. If the weather stays smooth, I will look for around 600 kg per mu.
